findings.impact: The pre-fix path allowed an authorized hostile MCP child to make catalog discovery consume more memory/tool objects than Semwright intended before the aggregate guard ran. No credential exposure or authority escalation was demonstrated.
preconditions: An owner has configured and authorized an external stdio MCP executable.
The upstream responds to tools/list with adversarial pagination.
The call remains within the outer timeout long enough to materialize multiple pages.
findings.recommended_remediation: Completed. Fix 4ef9a06e applies incremental tool/page/cursor-cycle bounds; a separate reviewer inspected the loop and verified two hosted sandboxed federation runs.
findings.residual_risk: The bounded-pagination remediation has separate-authorship revalidation for R16 closure. This does not prove absence of every resource-exhaustion path or make upstream MCPs trusted.
findings.severity_basis: A hostile owner-configured MCP server could keep returning paginated tool catalogs/cursors so rmcp 3.4.1 accumulated entries before Semwright applied its 512-tool aggregate check. The existing 10-second timeout bounded time but not incremental memory/catalog materialization.
findings.title: Federated MCP tools/list aggregation was bounded only after unbounded pagination
